newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin back in Kremlin to meet senior judge.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin back in Kremlin to meet senior judge.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin went to the Kremlin on Thursday for the third time since he left hospital last week following treatment for pneumonia.
The presidential press office said Yeltsin, 65, was meeting Vladimir Tumanov, the head of Russia's constitutional court.
Yeltsin last went to the Kremlin on Tuesday to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Ivan Korotchenya, secretary of the 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States.
But he has appeared just once on television since he was taken ill on January 6, prompting speculation that his recovery is slower and less complete than aides say.
Yeltsin looked alert but thin in Tuesday's brief television footage. But the film was heavily edited, making it difficult to judge the president's state of health.
Yeltsin, ill first with heart problems last year and then with pneumonia, has spent only a few days at his Kremlin desk since he won a second term in office on July 3.

Interfax news agency quoted presidential press secretary Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying Yeltsin and Tumanov would discuss ways to strengthen both the constitutional court and Russia's state structures.

The constitution gives the president far-reaching powers. Amendments would be possible only after prolonged debates in both houses of parliament, and some changes would have to be put to a referendum.
Aides say the president is busy preparing an address to both houses of the Russian parliament.
Chernomyrdin, his deputy under the constitution, left Moscow on Wednesday to attend the World Economic Forum in the Swiss mountain resort of Davos.
